headline: Financials and Chips Lead a Broad Retreat While Software Holds Its Ground
body_html:
Monday's session was a one-sided affair. Of the 665 stocks in our universe, only 158 finished higher and 502 fell. The damage was concentrated: financials dropped 5.84% and semiconductors lost 5.2%, the two deepest sector declines on the board.

The rotation was toward relative safety in software. The group slipped just 0.44%, the smallest loss of any sector we track, and several of its names rose outright. HubSpot gained 6.77%, Qualys added 5.24% and Freshworks climbed 4.42%. Energy fell 3.14% as reports of recovering Middle East exports pushed crude lower. Materials gave up 2.19%, while industrials, healthcare, consumer and homebuilders each lost between 1.0% and 1.41%.

The session's biggest casualty was Bullish, down 12.21%. The crypto exchange sank as bitcoin suffered a forced-selling cascade, and it set the tone for a punishing day in financials. Chip-related names also took heavy hits: Applied Optoelectronics fell 9.48% and Tower Semiconductor 9.17%. When selling is this lopsided, the stocks that merely stand still can be the most telling. Tuesday's session will show whether software's resilience is a real shift or just a pause.

briefs.headline: Crypto Liquidations Rattle Exchange Stocks
briefs.body: Bitcoin slid sharply during the session after a wave of forced selling, then recovered only a little. The shakeout hit crypto-linked equities hardest, with Bullish shedding 12.21%, the steepest drop among the names we track.

briefs.headline: Crude Eases as Middle East Supply Returns
briefs.body: U.S. oil prices fell as exports from the Middle East showed signs of recovery. Energy stocks followed, dropping 3.14% as a group. That ranked third-worst among our sectors, behind only financials and semiconductors.

briefs.headline: Cybersecurity and CRM Names Buck the Selloff
briefs.body: Software was the most resilient group in a weak tape, falling only 0.44%. Qualys rose 5.24% and Freshworks 4.42%, while HubSpot led all gainers at 6.77%. Investors appeared to favor these names while selling elsewhere.

briefs.headline: Diagnostics Makers Sell Off Sharply
briefs.body: Two genetic-testing and diagnostics companies landed among the session's worst performers. Natera fell 9.59% and Caris Life Sciences dropped 8.85%. Healthcare overall lost 1.33%, so the weakness in this niche was far steeper than in the broader group.

briefs.headline: Bank of Canada's Macklem Plans to Step Aside
briefs.body: Governor Tiff Macklem will leave his post when his term ends in 2027, Reuters reported. The announcement begins the search for a successor at the central bank, and investors will watch who is chosen and how they approach monetary policy.

briefs.headline: Tanker Rates Tumble From Record Peaks
briefs.body: Rates for supertankers have dropped by more than 60% from their record highs, Reuters reported. The slide fits a picture of oil logistics normalizing as Middle East exports recover, though conditions in the region remain unsettled.
